overview: 56 new pieces in the last 48 hours across 12 sources. Most of it is about software engineering, AI tools, AI research.

reads.title: [AINews] Google admits AI Mode hurts Search revenue; -15% $500B drop worst since 2004 IPO. AI Bear Market coming?
reads.author: swyx .ai
reads.description: It turns out you cannot have your cake AND eat it
reads.summary: As an engineer-focused newsletter we only very rarely let financial stories through (our last example was Jan 2025 ), but when this is about the future of Google and Google Search , with a recently departed AI leadership, you cannot not care. At its heart is the tension between overview pages and underlying pages they summarize.

reads.title: Was I wrong about open models & cyber risks?
reads.author: Nathan Lambert
reads.description: Last week coined the term “Black October“ after an onslaught of critical vulnerability disclosures, including PHP2Shell and GitLab, signified the moment when the cyber risks of AI models started to materialize.
reads.summary: Last week coined the term “ Black October “ after an onslaught of critical vulnerability disclosures, including PHP2Shell and GitLab, signified the moment when the cyber risks of AI models started to materialize. It seemed like the news cycle had stabilized a bit when I started writing this, but then there was news about another major crypto security incident at Binance .

reads.title: [AINews] Building AIE CODE: The top Coding Agent Conference
reads.author: swyx .ai
reads.description: Mistral’s open-weight release, frontier monitoring, and the day’s AI Twitter and Reddit recaps.
reads.summary: It’s a quiet day, so as we have done once per conference, we’ll do a behind the scenes look at AI Engineer , now serving 6M views a month for 1.8M monthly unique viewers . CODE is the last flagship AIE of the year (there are also 2 partner conferences coming up - AIEi Shanghai takes place next week, and AIEi Sydney is a side event of NeurIPS in December).

reads.description: dbreunig/nesformer Inspired by qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal, Drew Breunig baked a working emulator for a Nintendo Entertainment System 6502 CPU into the weights of Qwen3.5-4B. reads.title: GPT-6.1 Terra Draws a Python Reading a Book
reads.description: Explore GPT-6.1 Terra's Python code, turtle drawing, and responses to small tasks that check modern syntax, release knowledge, focused edits, and made-up functions.
reads.summary: We asked GPT-6.1 Terra to draw a python reading a book using the turtle module. It’s one of five tasks in Real Python’s informal model comparison , which explores how models handle everyday Python work.

reads.title: Webhook IP ranges added to the Meta API
reads.author: Allison
reads.description: We’re adding IP ranges for GitHub webhook deliveries on github.com. The Meta API now includes these additional ranges in the hooks field. If you maintain a static network allowlist for… The post Webhook IP ranges added to the Meta API appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
reads.summary: We’re adding IP ranges for GitHub webhook deliveries on github.com. The Meta API now includes these additional ranges in the hooks field.

reads.title: Learn With Mentor AI: A Guided Journey Through Async Python
reads.description: Experience a new way of learning on Real Python by working through async Python in conversation with Mentor AI, one well-placed question at a time.
reads.summary: I’d been writing Python for a couple of years before async programming made sense to me. I understood the general idea, but the syntax just never felt like Python.
